blast_huc12.name: Long Creek
blast_huc12.receiving_river: Skunk River at Augusta (USGS 05474000, 6.2 km S) -> Mississippi River (~15 km SE)
blast_huc12.superfund_context: IAAAP has been an EPA National Priorities List (Superfund) site since 1990 with long-term surface-water and groundwater monitoring along Brush Creek, Long Creek, and Spring Creek.

epa_sampling_campaign.lab_turnaround_note: EPA Xact air telemetry updates in near-real-time; physical soil, surface-wipe, water, and air-cassette ICP-MS lab samples typically require 24-72+ hours for validated upload.
epa_sampling_campaign.independent_testing: Purdue University (Dr. Ellen Wells, School of Health Sciences) is also offering free before/after residential soil & dust lead testing for Iowa residents.

municipal_water_sources.source: 80% Mississippi River (upstream of Skunk River confluence) + 20% Pleistocene aquifer wells
municipal_water_sources.exposure_pathway: Upwind of air plume & upstream of Skunk River outfall
Upwind (N/NW) of SW plume; deep/cased wells insulated from surface dust

municipal_water_sources.source: Mississippi Alluvial Aquifer wells treated via Reverse Osmosis (RO)
municipal_water_sources.exposure_pathway: East edge of SW plume; RO treatment removes >95-99% of dissolved/particulate lead

municipal_water_sources.source: Municipal groundwater wells & Rathbun Regional Water
municipal_water_sources.exposure_pathway: Under SW air plume (modeled surface dust <=0.2 ug/ft^2); cased wells shielded from airborne dust

municipal_water_sources.source: 100% Mississippi River surface water (downstream of Skunk & Des Moines confluences)
municipal_water_sources.exposure_pathway: Massive Mississippi River dilution (~40,000-60,000 cfs) + conventional coagulation/filtration removes particulate lead

municipal_water_sources.city: Private Rural Wells & Livestock Ponds (0-5 mi SW)
municipal_water_sources.source: Shallow private wells, cisterns, open farm ponds along Long/Brush Creek & Augusta
municipal_water_sources.exposure_pathway: Primary focus of EPA's 210 water samples; open ponds/cisterns could catch settled dust if uncovered, while Long Creek runoff is the main medium-term watchpoint
